lessons.content_en:
Stand magnifiers are optical near-vision devices in which a support maintains a relatively fixed distance between the lens and the reading material. This can simplify focusing for people with reduced hand control or tremor. The patient generally moves the material or device to explore the text, while the prescribed near correction and working distance must still be considered. Some stand magnifiers are designed for use with spectacle correction; others have a built-in viewing arrangement. Illumination may be integrated or external, but reflections and glare must be checked. Higher-power stand magnifiers usually provide a smaller field and shorter focal distance. Assess posture, line tracking, print size, contrast and sustained reading speed rather than selecting by labelled power alone.

Clinical application
Begin with a clearly defined activity and document baseline performance using the patient's habitual correction and usual environment. Optimize reversible factors before introducing an aid. Demonstrate the device or strategy, allow supervised practice, and record measurable changes in speed, accuracy, comfort, independence and safety.

Clinical reasoning
Device selection is not determined by visual acuity alone. Interpret findings with visual field, contrast sensitivity, ocular alignment, cognition, dexterity, hearing, posture, motivation and environmental demands. A device that performs well in the clinic may fail at home if its controls, portability or maintenance are unsuitable. Coordinate referral when medical instability or additional rehabilitation needs are identified.

Key points
• Match the intervention to a specific functional goal.
• Consider field, contrast, posture and handling as well as acuity.
• Train the patient in realistic conditions.
• Reassess measurable outcomes and revise the plan when needed.
lessons.content_ar:
المكبر ذو القاعدة يثبت المسافة بين العدسة ومادة القراءة، وده بيساعد المريض الذي يعاني من رعشة أو ضعف التحكم باليد. أحياناً يحرك المريض المادة تحت المكبر بدلاً من تحريك العدسة، مع ضرورة مراعاة تصحيح القريب ومسافة العمل. بعض الأنواع تحتاج نظارة القريب، وأخرى لها نظام مشاهدة مختلف. الإضاءة المدمجة قد تكون مفيدة لكن يجب فحص الانعكاسات والوهج. كلما زادت القوة غالباً صغر المجال وقصرت المسافة البؤرية. الاختيار الصحيح يعتمد على وضعية المريض وتتبع السطور وسرعة القراءة المستمرة، وليس رقم القوة المكتوب فقط.

التطبيق السريري
ابدأ بنشاط محدد ووثق الأداء الأساسي باستخدام التصحيح المعتاد وبيئة المريض الطبيعية. حسّن العوامل القابلة للتعديل قبل إدخال الوسيلة. اعرض الجهاز أو الاستراتيجية، واترك للمريض فرصة للتدرب تحت الإشراف، ثم سجل التغير في السرعة والدقة والراحة والاستقلالية والسلامة.

التفكير السريري
لا يعتمد اختيار الوسيلة على حدة البصر وحدها. فسر النتائج مع المجال البصري وحساسية التباين ومحاذاة العين والإدراك والبراعة والسمع والوضعية والدافعية ومتطلبات البيئة. قد ينجح الجهاز في العيادة ويفشل في المنزل إذا كانت أزراره أو قابليته للحمل أو صيانته غير مناسبة. نسق الإحالة عند وجود عدم استقرار طبي أو احتياجات تأهيلية إضافية.

نقاط أساسية
• طابق التدخل مع هدف وظيفي محدد.
• راعِ المجال والتباين والوضعية وسهولة الاستخدام إلى جانب الحدة.
• درّب المريض في ظروف واقعية.
• أعد قياس النتائج وعدّل الخطة عند الحاجة.

lessons.content_en:
High-addition spectacles provide substantial plus power for close near tasks and allow hands-free use. The increased dioptric power requires a short working distance, commonly demanding careful posture and a stable reading position. The near focal distance is approximately the reciprocal of the add power in metres, although effective use also depends on vertex distance, lens design and the patient's refractive status. High adds may be prescribed binocularly or monocularly according to acuity, field, alignment and comfort. They are less suitable for tasks requiring frequent changes of viewing distance or broad mobility. Training should include positioning, illumination, scanning and safe use of the restricted working range.

Clinical application
Begin with a clearly defined activity and document baseline performance using the patient's habitual correction and usual environment. Optimize reversible factors before introducing an aid. Demonstrate the device or strategy, allow supervised practice, and record measurable changes in speed, accuracy, comfort, independence and safety.

Interpret findings with visual field, contrast sensitivity, ocular alignment, cognition, dexterity, hearing, posture, motivation and environmental demands. A device that performs well in the clinic may fail at home if its controls, portability or maintenance are unsuitable. Coordinate referral when medical instability or additional rehabilitation needs are identified.

Key points
• Match the intervention to a specific functional goal.
• Consider field, contrast, posture and handling as well as acuity.
• Train the patient in realistic conditions.
• Reassess measurable outcomes and revise the plan when needed.

النظارات ذات الإضافة العالية توفر قوة موجبة كبيرة للقراءة القريبة وتترك اليدين حرتين. لكنها تفرض مسافة عمل قصيرة، لذلك تحتاج وضعية جلوس مناسبة وثباتاً أثناء القراءة. المسافة البؤرية النظرية تقارب مقلوب قوة الإضافة بالمتر، لكن الاستخدام الفعلي يتأثر بمسافة العدسة عن العين وتصميمها والانكسار. يمكن وصفها للعينين أو لعين واحدة حسب الحدة والمجال والمحاذاة والراحة. لا تناسب المهام التي تتطلب تغييراً متكرراً في مسافة النظر أو حركة واسعة. التدريب يشمل التموضع والإضاءة ومسح السطر واحترام مجال العمل المحدود.

lessons.content_en:
Telescopes are used in low vision to enlarge the apparent angular size of distant targets such as signs, classroom boards and presentation screens. They may be monocular or binocular and can be handheld, spectacle-mounted or bioptic. Magnification is achieved at the cost of a narrower field of view, reduced depth-of-field and increased sensitivity to alignment and movement. A telescope is generally best for brief spotting rather than continuous mobility. Distance refraction, ocular dominance, field status, posture, target distance and task demands influence selection. Training must address locating the target, focusing, steady positioning, scanning and safe transition between telescope and unaided viewing. Driving use is subject to local legal and clinical requirements and cannot be assumed safe from device possession alone.

Clinical application
Begin with a clearly defined activity and document baseline performance using the patient's habitual correction and usual environment. Optimize reversible factors before introducing an aid. Demonstrate the device or strategy, allow supervised practice, and record measurable changes in speed, accuracy, comfort, independence and safety.

Clinical reasoning
Device selection is not determined by visual acuity alone. Interpret findings with visual field, contrast sensitivity, ocular alignment, cognition, dexterity, hearing, posture, motivation and environmental demands. A device that performs well in the clinic may fail at home if its controls, portability or maintenance are unsuitable. Coordinate referral when medical instability or additional rehabilitation needs are identified.

Key points
• Match the intervention to a specific functional goal.
• Consider field, contrast, posture and handling as well as acuity.
• Train the patient in realistic conditions.
• Reassess measurable outcomes and revise the plan when needed.

تستخدم المناظير لتكبير الأهداف البعيدة مثل اللوحات والإشارات وشاشة المحاضرة. قد تكون أحادية أو ثنائية، يدوية أو مثبتة بالنظارة أو بنظام bioptic. التكبير يأتي على حساب تضييق مجال الرؤية وتقليل عمق المجال وزيادة حساسية الجهاز للمحاذاة والحركة. لذلك تناسب غالباً الرؤية السريعة للهدف وليس التنقل المستمر. الاختيار يتأثر بانكسار البعيد والعين المسيطرة والمجال والوضعية والمسافة وطبيعة المهمة. التدريب ضروري لتحديد الهدف والتركيز والتثبيت والمسح والانتقال الآمن للرؤية دون المنظار. استخدام المنظار أثناء القيادة يخضع للقوانين والتقييم السريري ولا يعني تلقائياً أن القيادة آمنة.

lessons.content_en:
Electronic magnification devices use a camera, display and image-processing controls to enlarge near or distance targets. Common functions include continuous magnification adjustment, contrast polarity changes, brightness control, freeze-frame, line guides and image capture. These features can improve access for people who need high magnification or customized contrast, but performance depends on display quality, latency, portability, battery life, dexterity and familiarity with the interface. Maximum magnification is not necessarily the most useful setting because it reduces the visible area and may make navigation difficult. Assess the patient's tasks, visual field, hand function, cognition, technology access and maintenance needs. Training should progress from basic focusing to contrast settings, reading navigation and independent operation.

Clinical application
Begin with a clearly defined activity and document baseline performance using the patient's habitual correction and usual environment. Optimize reversible factors before introducing an aid. Demonstrate the device or strategy, allow supervised practice, and record measurable changes in speed, accuracy, comfort, independence and safety.

Clinical reasoning
Device selection is not determined by visual acuity alone. Interpret findings with visual field, contrast sensitivity, ocular alignment, cognition, dexterity, hearing, posture, motivation and environmental demands. A device that performs well in the clinic may fail at home if its controls, portability or maintenance are unsuitable. Coordinate referral when medical instability or additional rehabilitation needs are identified.

Key points
• Match the intervention to a specific functional goal.
• Consider field, contrast, posture and handling as well as acuity.
• Train the patient in realistic conditions.
• Reassess measurable outcomes and revise the plan when needed.

lessons.content_en:
Video magnifiers, historically called closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems, display a magnified camera image on a monitor. Desktop systems may provide a stable platform for prolonged reading, writing, medication handling and detailed near tasks. Camera-to-object distance, monitor size, working space, image resolution, contrast modes and control layout affect performance. Some systems support distance viewing or split-screen functions. The user must learn to position the material, control magnification, move across lines and use guides without losing place. Excessive magnification can reduce context and increase navigation time. Selection should be based on the actual task, available space, portability requirements, visual field and the user's ability to operate controls.

Clinical application
Begin with a clearly defined activity and document baseline performance using the patient's habitual correction and usual environment. Optimize reversible factors before introducing an aid. Demonstrate the device or strategy, allow supervised practice, and record measurable changes in speed, accuracy, comfort, independence and safety.

Clinical reasoning
Device selection is not determined by visual acuity alone. Interpret findings with visual field, contrast sensitivity, ocular alignment, cognition, dexterity, hearing, posture, motivation and environmental demands. A device that performs well in the clinic may fail at home if its controls, portability or maintenance are unsuitable. Coordinate referral when medical instability or additional rehabilitation needs are identified.

Key points
• Match the intervention to a specific functional goal.
• Consider field, contrast, posture and handling as well as acuity.
• Train the patient in realistic conditions.
• Reassess measurable outcomes and revise the plan when needed.
lessons.content_ar:

lessons.content_en:
Digital accessibility enables people with low vision to use electronic information through adaptable presentation and assistive functions. Useful features include operating-system magnification, screen readers, text resizing, high-contrast themes, cursor enlargement, speech output, reflow, zoom and adjustable spacing. Screen magnification enlarges visual content but may require panning; screen readers provide auditory access and can be valuable when visual reading is inefficient. Compatibility, language support, keyboard navigation, app design and user preference influence success. A clinician should identify the task and demonstrate relevant built-in features without assuming that every patient is comfortable with technology. Training should include privacy, passwords, safe online behaviour and a plan for technical support.

Clinical application
Begin with a clearly defined activity and document baseline performance using the patient's habitual correction and usual environment. Optimize reversible factors before introducing an aid. Demonstrate the device or strategy, allow supervised practice, and record measurable changes in speed, accuracy, comfort, independence and safety.

Clinical reasoning
Device selection is not determined by visual acuity alone. Interpret findings with visual field, contrast sensitivity, ocular alignment, cognition, dexterity, hearing, posture, motivation and environmental demands. A device that performs well in the clinic may fail at home if its controls, portability or maintenance are unsuitable. Coordinate referral when medical instability or additional rehabilitation needs are identified.

Key points
• Match the intervention to a specific functional goal.
• Consider field, contrast, posture and handling as well as acuity.
• Train the patient in realistic conditions.
• Reassess measurable outcomes and revise the plan when needed.

lessons.content_en:
Non-optical aids improve task performance by modifying the environment, materials or method rather than enlarging the retinal image. Examples include task lighting, reading stands, bold-line paper, felt-tip pens, tactile markings, large-print labels, talking clocks, audio books, signature guides and organizational strategies. These interventions may be inexpensive and can complement optical devices. Their suitability depends on the task, motor ability, cognition, hearing, tactile sensitivity and home or workplace environment. Environmental modifications should reduce clutter, improve contrast, standardize item locations and minimize fall hazards. Demonstrate each aid in context and assess whether it improves independence, speed, accuracy or safety.

Coordinate referral when medical instability or additional rehabilitation needs are identified.

• Match the intervention to a specific functional goal.
• Consider field, contrast, posture and handling as well as acuity.

• Reassess measurable outcomes and revise the plan when needed.

lessons.content_en:
Eccentric viewing is a learned strategy in which a person with central visual loss directs the target toward a usable retinal area away from the damaged fovea. The patient develops a consistent gaze position that places the object on a more functional retinal region. Training may use fixation targets, letters, words and progressively meaningful tasks. Performance is influenced by scotoma size and location, residual peripheral sensitivity, eye movements, cognition and motivation. Eccentric viewing is not the same as restoring the fovea, and it does not guarantee a stable or optimal retinal locus in every patient. Assessment and training should be individualized, with realistic goals and repeated functional evaluation.

Clinical application
Begin with a clearly defined activity and document baseline performance using the patient's habitual correction and usual environment. Optimize reversible factors before introducing an aid. Demonstrate the device or strategy, allow supervised practice, and record measurable changes in speed, accuracy, comfort, independence and safety.

Clinical reasoning
Device selection is not determined by visual acuity alone. Interpret findings with visual field, contrast sensitivity, ocular alignment, cognition, dexterity, hearing, posture, motivation and environmental demands. A device that performs well in the clinic may fail at home if its controls, portability or maintenance are unsuitable. Coordinate referral when medical instability or additional rehabilitation needs are identified.

Key points
• Match the intervention to a specific functional goal.
• Consider field, contrast, posture and handling as well as acuity.
• Train the patient in realistic conditions.
• Reassess measurable outcomes and revise the plan when needed.

النظر اللامركزي استراتيجية يتعلم فيها المريض المصاب بفقدان الرؤية المركزية توجيه الهدف نحو منطقة شبكية قابلة للاستخدام بعيداً عن النقرة المتضررة. يتدرب على اتجاه نظر ثابت نسبياً بحيث تقع الصورة على منطقة شبكية أكثر كفاءة. يبدأ التدريب بأهداف التثبيت والحروف والكلمات ثم مهام ذات معنى. تتأثر النتيجة بحجم العتمة وموقعها والحساسية الطرفية المتبقية وحركات العين والإدراك والدافعية. هذه الاستراتيجية لا تعيد وظيفة النقرة ولا تضمن وجود موضع مثالي ثابت لدى الجميع. لذلك يجب تخصيص التدريب ووضع أهداف واقعية وإعادة تقييم الأداء.

lessons.content_en:
A preferred retinal locus (PRL) is an extrafoveal retinal area that a person habitually uses for fixation when the fovea is impaired. It may develop spontaneously and can differ between tasks or viewing conditions. A PRL is identified through fixation assessment, often using microperimetry or other suitable techniques, and should be interpreted with the location of the scotoma and residual retinal sensitivity. The PRL is not necessarily the most efficient location for reading or face recognition. Rehabilitation may aim to improve awareness, consistency and use of a functional locus, or to train an alternative locus when appropriate. Outcomes should be measured by task performance rather than assuming that anatomical location alone predicts success.

Clinical application
Begin with a clearly defined activity and document baseline performance using the patient's habitual correction and usual environment. Optimize reversible factors before introducing an aid. Demonstrate the device or strategy, allow supervised practice, and record measurable changes in speed, accuracy, comfort, independence and safety.

Clinical reasoning
Device selection is not determined by visual acuity alone. Interpret findings with visual field, contrast sensitivity, ocular alignment, cognition, dexterity, hearing, posture, motivation and environmental demands. A device that performs well in the clinic may fail at home if its controls, portability or maintenance are unsuitable. Coordinate referral when medical instability or additional rehabilitation needs are identified.

Key points
• Match the intervention to a specific functional goal.
• Consider field, contrast, posture and handling as well as acuity.
• Train the patient in realistic conditions.
• Reassess measurable outcomes and revise the plan when needed.

lessons.content_en:
Reading rehabilitation combines optical, electronic, environmental and learned strategies to improve access to print. Begin by identifying the patient's priority materials, reading goals, endurance, language, literacy level and preferred format. Establish baseline reading speed, accuracy, critical print size, comprehension and symptoms. Interventions may include appropriate near correction, magnification, contrast enhancement, task lighting, line guides, eccentric viewing, electronic text and audio alternatives. Training should progress from short meaningful passages to sustained reading, with planned rest and ergonomic adjustments. A successful outcome is not simply the ability to decipher smaller print; it is improved participation in personally important reading activities.

Clinical application
Begin with a clearly defined activity and document baseline performance using the patient's habitual correction and usual environment. Optimize reversible factors before introducing an aid. Demonstrate the device or strategy, allow supervised practice, and record measurable changes in speed, accuracy, comfort, independence and safety.

Clinical reasoning
Device selection is not determined by visual acuity alone. Interpret findings with visual field, contrast sensitivity, ocular alignment, cognition, dexterity, hearing, posture, motivation and environmental demands. A device that performs well in the clinic may fail at home if its controls, portability or maintenance are unsuitable. Coordinate referral when medical instability or additional rehabilitation needs are identified.

Key points
• Match the intervention to a specific functional goal.
• Consider field, contrast, posture and handling as well as acuity.
• Train the patient in realistic conditions.
• Reassess measurable outcomes and revise the plan when needed.
lessons.content_ar:
إعادة التأهيل القرائي تجمع الوسائل البصرية والإلكترونية وتعديل البيئة والاستراتيجيات المكتسبة لتحسين الوصول إلى النص. نبدأ بتحديد المواد التي تهم المريض وأهداف القراءة والتحمل واللغة ومستوى القراءة والصيغة المفضلة. نسجل السرعة والدقة وحجم الطباعة الحرج والفهم والأعراض قبل التدخل. قد تشمل الخطة تصحيح القريب والتكبير وتحسين التباين وإضاءة المهمة وأدلة السطور والنظر اللامركزي والنص الإلكتروني والبدائل الصوتية. يتدرج التدريب من مقاطع قصيرة ذات معنى إلى قراءة مستمرة، مع فترات راحة وتعديل الوضعية. النجاح ليس مجرد قراءة حروف أصغر، بل تحسن المشاركة في أنشطة القراءة المهمة للمريض.

التطبيق السريري
ابدأ بنشاط محدد ووثق الأداء الأساسي باستخدام التصحيح المعتاد وبيئة المريض الطبيعية. حسّن العوامل القابلة للتعديل قبل إدخال الوسيلة. اعرض الجهاز أو الاستراتيجية، واترك للمريض فرصة للتدرب تحت الإشراف، ثم سجل التغير في السرعة والدقة والراحة والاستقلالية والسلامة.

التفكير السريري
لا يعتمد اختيار الوسيلة على حدة البصر وحدها. فسر النتائج مع المجال البصري وحساسية التباين ومحاذاة العين والإدراك والبراعة والسمع والوضعية والدافعية ومتطلبات البيئة. قد ينجح الجهاز في العيادة ويفشل في المنزل إذا كانت أزراره أو قابليته للحمل أو صيانته غير مناسبة. نسق الإحالة عند وجود عدم استقرار طبي أو احتياجات تأهيلية إضافية.

نقاط أساسية
• طابق التدخل مع هدف وظيفي محدد.
• راعِ المجال والتباين والوضعية وسهولة الاستخدام إلى جانب الحدة.
• درّب المريض في ظروف واقعية.
• أعد قياس النتائج وعدّل الخطة عند الحاجة.

questions.question_en: The first step in reading rehabilitation is to:
questions.explanation_en: Rehabilitation must begin with meaningful patient-centred goals.
questions.explanation_ar: يجب أن يبدأ التأهيل بأهداف مهمة للمريض.

options.option_en: Identify the patient's reading goals and materials

questions.question_en: Which measure is useful at baseline?
questions.explanation_en: Baseline measures allow comparison after intervention.
questions.explanation_ar: القياسات الأساسية تسمح بالمقارنة بعد التدخل.

questions.question_en: Which intervention may be included in a reading plan?
questions.explanation_en: A combined approach addresses multiple barriers to reading.
questions.explanation_ar: النهج المتكامل يعالج عدة عوائق للقراءة.

questions.question_en: Why use graded reading practice?
questions.explanation_en: Progression supports adaptation and sustainable reading.
questions.explanation_ar: التدرج يدعم التكيف والتحمل المستمر.

options.option_en: To build endurance and skill progressively

questions.question_en: The most meaningful outcome is:
questions.explanation_en: Participation and task success matter more than a single chart result.
questions.explanation_ar: المشاركة والنجاح في المهمة أهم من نتيجة لوحة واحدة.

options.option_en: Improved participation in personally important reading
Ability to read the smallest chart line once
